title: A new mixed-integer linear programming model for ultimate pit limit determination and production planning of open pit mines considering effective operational constraints
core_idea: Develop a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model to determine the ultimate pit limit and perform long-term production scheduling for open-pit mines that maximizes project net present value while enforcing seven operational constraints (four geometric: block precedence, pit floor width, block extraction continuity, non-repetition of block selection; and three demand-based: extraction capacity, ore block requirement, minimum feed grade per period). The model supports scenarios with and without a mine stockpile, incorporates stockpile inventory and shortage variables to handle demand-production mismatches, and is implemented in GAMS for testing on a hypothetical block dataset.
tldr: A MILP model is proposed to determine ultimate pit limits and optimize long-term open-pit mine production scheduling (with optional stockpile handling) under key geometric and demand-based operational constraints to maximize NPV.
